articles.title: Pressure review – stormy weather in tense D-day forecast retelling
articles.summary: Andrew Scott finds levels of complexity in a stoic character based on meteorologist James Stagg, the man who persuaded Eisenhower to delay Operation Overlord, for this slick wartime drama.
body: This is to the rage of Col Irving P Krick (Chris Messina), the swaggeringly gung-ho American meteorologist who has always had Ike’s confidence until now. And if we were unsure about this character’s brash-Yank status, in his opening scene he literally shimmies and bops to the Andrews Sisters’ Boogie-Woogie Bugle Boy in the operations room to the uptight, thin-lipped astonishment of Stagg who, as overall commanding officer, tells the Americans to get that piano out of there.

Krick figures they’re good to go on the 5 June, and Stagg’s obduracy also enrages the drawlingly contemptuous General Montgomery (Damien Lewis), who is mustard keen to get boots on the beach pronto. Everyone thinks they need to move right now. Stagg thinks they need to wait. But if he’s wrong, tens of thousands of personnel will die. And to top it off, his wife back in London is nine months pregnant. Pressure fronts of all sorts are closing in.

articles.title: ‘He goes to the dark side’: behind the scenes on the Shaun the Sheep horror movie
articles.summary: Aardman’s hero is back in The Beast of Mossy Bottom – a terrifying tale of frankenfood, pitchfork-wielding villagers and a monster with suspiciously stiff orange hair. Our writer meets its makers and moulds her very own Shaun.
body: The Aztec West industrial estate in Bristol was opened by Margaret Thatcher in December 1989. One hundred and sixty acres of breeze block and mirrored glass, it is home to about 7,000 employees and 100 companies, including EDF, EE, HSBC, Co-op Legal and Spandex. It has its own gym, spa, church and morgue. Step inside Unit 1410, though, and bucolic England is magically restored. A farm complete with sheep. Rolling fields in autumn colours. A small parish town boasting post office, war memorial, chippy. It looks lush. But before you hit up Rightmove, I should say: Mossingham is only two feet tall. And plasticine.

It’s January 2026 and Aardman animations are about halfway through production on Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom. The 300-odd staff in this shed are full speed ahead – which means each of the 30 animators is rattling out almost two seconds of footage a day.
points: Aardman’s hero is back in The Beast of Mossy Bottom – a terrifying tale of frankenfood, pitchfork-wielding villagers and a monster with suspiciously stiff orange hair.
Our writer meets its makers and moulds her very own Shaun.

articles.title: La Femme Infidèle review – Chabrol’s eerie domestic thriller is a brilliant ballet of repression and fear
articles.summary: Claude Chabrol’s 1969 film charts a complex marriage in which a husband suspects his wife is cheating on him. Writer-director Claude Chabrol’s eerie 1969 masterpiece of frozen emotions and unspoken truths is now rereleased, alongside a Chabrol season at London’s BFI Southbank.
body: So Charles engages a private detective who finds the man’s address and Charles goes there, smilingly assuring the astonished Victor that his wife gave him the details and that he has always been fully au courant with this situation. All he wants is a civilised chat. Victor relaxes. But what exactly did Charles want to do at this meeting? Perhaps he really did only intend to luxuriate masochistically in the details, which Victor will incautiously reveal. This would also appear to be why Charles organises a party at a nightclub with friends, where he can inspect his wife’s behaviour with other men.

Does Hélène know that he knows? Perhaps what she knows is that she doesn’t care what he knows. Yet Chabrol allows us once to penetrate her mask of elegant detachment. After sex one afternoon, Hélène and Victor find themselves talking about their respective children and we see her realisation that Charles could not live without his son and she couldn’t live without the boy either. That is what divorce would mean. The end of this illicit relationship has ironically begun right then and there.

articles.title: Serbian Sci-Fi Epic ‘Sanctuary,’ Starring ‘The Handmaid’s Tale’s’ Nina Kiri, Acquired for U.S. Distribution (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Vertical has acquired U.S. distribution rights to “Sanctuary,” an English-language, post-apocalyptic thriller starring “The Handmaid’s Tale’s” Nina Kiri. According to the synopsis, “Sanctuary” is set on a post-apocalyptic Earth, where the discovery of a cryogenically suspended woman provokes fear…
body: “The time is near enough so the events that led to the collapse of civilization are still relevant, but far enough that they have been shrouded in mystery and myth,” the director said. “The intent was to make an entertaining genre film that explores the cyclical nature of history and the individual’s role inside it.”

Producer Đorđe Stanković, of Belgrade-based Void Pictures, said that the filmmakers “set out to make an ambitious science-fiction film from Serbia that could speak to an international audience without losing its own identity.”

“Producing the film was an enormous undertaking, but also proof that genre cinema of this scale can come from this part of Europe,” he said. “We’re incredibly proud of what the team created and excited for the film to now begin its journey to audiences around the world.”

Void’s Vukota Antunović added: “From the beginning, ‘Sanctuary’ was driven by a shared belief in the story and the world we were building. Bringing together an international and domestic cast and a remarkable Serbian crew allowed us to make something that feels both rooted here and genuinely global.”

articles.summary: Future series will no longer be broadcast on BBC Three as the show moves to a streaming platform owned by its production company.
body: RuPaul's Drag Race UK is leaving the BBC after eight series, the broadcaster has confirmed.
A spokesperson for the broadcaster said it was facing "very difficult choices" in the face of "significant financial pressures".

The show is currently broadcast on BBC Three and iPlayer. Future series - as well as its spin-off vs The World - will be broadcast on Wow Presents Plus, a streaming platform owned by the production company behind the show.
At its peak, the UK version of the international drag competition averaged at around 1.5 million viewers per episode.

articles.title: Russian director refuses to denounce lead actor despite criticism from Ukraine
articles.summary: Ilya Khrzhanovsky’s DAU, about physicist Lev Landau, stars Russian conductor Teodor Currentzis, who has refused to speak out against Putin’s war. The director of a controversial new Russian film has said “everyone pays for his own choice” when asked about his lead’s refusal to condemn Russia’s war…
body: In film-maker Ilya Khrzhanovsky’s DAU, which premiered at the Venice film festival on Wednesday, Greek-Russian star conductor Teodor Currentzis plays the eponymously nicknamed protagonist, Nobel prize-winning quantum physicist Lev Landau.

In the run-up to the festival, the film’s inclusion in the lineup was heavily criticised by the Ukrainian ministry of foreign affairs, in part over the fact that Athens-born Currentzis continues to live and work in Russia, and has never publicly denounced Putin’s war.

“It’s his choice,” Khrzhanovsky said at a press conference on the Lido. “But I think everyone is paying for his own choice, his own life, his own destiny,” added the film-maker, who has renounced his Russian citizenship over the full-scale invasion and lives in exile in Germany.

He referred to his film, in which Currentzis’s character Landau is put under pressure to work on the development of the nuclear bomb and eventually reluctantly agrees. “As you can see in the movie, the main character is also making different choices, and he’s paying for his choices.”

articles.title: ‘Crew Girl’ Review: Netflix’s Latest YA Sports Drama Checks All the Expected Boxes, but Not Much More
articles.summary: Starring Miku Martineau and Jessica Paré, the series follows a female rower who begins serving as coxswain for the boys' team after transferring to an elite New England prep school.
body: As far as bingeable YA dramas go, Crew Girl is probably good enough. Following an elite teenage rower, Teagan (Miku Martineau), who joins the varsity boys’ crew team at a new school, Vivian Lin and Morwyn Brebner’s new Netflix series hits all the expected marks — filthy-rich mean kids, intrafamily feuds, an angsty love triangle and many pretty shots of lakes — breezily enough to consume over a weekend for viewers who can’t get enough of this specific and very prolific genre.

Unlike some sports shows (even some very good ones ), the series does not treat athletics as incidental, but as the very sun around which this entire verdant and sun-dappled universe revolves. The premiere shows us the inside of an Easton Prep classroom for the first and last time, and does the expository work of explaining that since this only recently coed institution has no girls’ rowing program for Teagan to join, her only way of getting on a boat is to serve as coxswain (the non-rowing member who helps steer and coordinate the team) for the boys.

articles.title: Mercedes Ron Discusses Prime Video’s New YA Romantic Thriller ‘Drawn Together’ and What’s Next for Her
articles.summary: The bestselling author, whose 'Fault' trilogy broke records, and Carolina Bang of Banijay-owned producer Pokeepsie Films share a busy outlook for the "House of Ron," including a first U.S. adaptation.
body: Banijay ‘s Pokeepsie Films and Amazon Prime Video continue to build out the “House of Ron,” the audiovisual empire of bestselling Argentine-born Spanish YA romance author Mercedes Ron.

The film adaptations of her popular enemies-to-lovers Culpables romance trilogy (Culpa Mía, Culpa Tuya, Culpa Nuestra) became not only the most-watched Spanish, but also the most-watched international original, for the streamer ever, with a combined 100 million views worldwide as of the summer.

On Wednesday, Prime premiered the first of two planned films based on another one of her hit novels in more than 240 countries and territories. Drawn Together is a romantic thriller, directed by Óscar Pedraza, that stars Ester Expósito ( Elite, The Wailing ) and Hugo Diego Garcia ( Death and Other Details, The Substance ). Expósito portrays Marfil Cortés, the New York City-based scion of a rich Spanish businessman. After being kidnapped, her father hires Sebastián Moore, played by Garcia, as a bodyguard to watch her. A strong mutual attraction develops as they deal with multiple threats back in Spain. Here is a trailer for the film.
